title: The Drowned Thorn
premise: Theo Villalobos, the last swordspeaker, has survived by hiding in Thornvale, a valley where magic cannot follow and their gift lies dormant. When crown hunters arrive seeking anyone with the gift, Theo flees with a dying elder's secret: the words in their blood can either wake or permanently silence the ancient thorn that once drowned a kingdom. Hunted across a realm that fears what it cannot control, Theo must choose between destroying their inheritance to live free, or speaking the oath and becoming the weapon everyone fears. In the end, Theo speaks a third oath no one taught them—one that binds the thorn to themselves alone—and returns to the valley changed, no longer hiding but guarding.
about_author: Mara Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath rituals before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people burdened by inherited duties they never asked for.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Establishes Thornvale's magic-dead quiet and Theo's unspoken oath, kept alive only through silent practice with a wooden blade. Emotional beat: restless contentment on the edge of fear.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: A peddler arrives bearing news: the crown has declared a hunt for the gifted. Theo's grandmother burns a hidden letter. POV Theo. Beat: dread settling like weather.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hands
chapters.summary: Grandmother Ilsa reveals fragments of the Villalobos lineage—oath-bound speakers who bound the Drowned Thorn centuries ago. POV Theo. Beat: awe tangled with resentment at years of lies.

chapters.title: The First Hunter
chapters.summary: A crown surveyor, Captain Ren Ostrev, arrives ostensibly mapping trade routes. His questions are too precise. POV alternating Theo/Ostrev. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension.

chapters.title: What the Blade Remembers
chapters.summary: Under pressure, Theo's gift stirs involuntarily—the wooden sword hums a single word. Ilsa witnesses it and goes pale. POV Theo. Beat: terror of one's own body.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday in Thornvale
chapters.summary: Ilsa burns the family archive, keeping only one page. She tells Theo: if hunters return, run east to the drowned city of Vaelmora. POV Ilsa, brief and elegiac. Beat: grief as preparation.

chapters.title: Ostrev's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ostrev's POV. He suspects Thornvale harbors a speaker and requests reinforcements, revealing his own motive: his brother died in a gifted uprising. Beat: antagonist made sympathetic.

chapters.title: The Night the Dogs Came
chapters.summary: Crown soldiers raid the village. Ilsa holds them off with a false confession; Theo escapes over the ridge as Thornvale burns behind them. POV Theo. Beat: survivor's guilt, sharp and immediate.

chapters.title: Eastward, Alone
chapters.summary: Theo crosses the magic-border for the first time; the gift floods back painfully—every word in sight has weight. POV Theo. Beat: disorientation and unwanted power.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Theo falls in with pilgrims, including Sefa, a sharp-tongued cartographer who notices Theo flinching at spoken blessings. POV Theo. Beat: wary first friendship.

chapters.title: Vaelmora Rising
chapters.summary: The drowned city emerges from the marsh at low tide, its towers wrapped in black thorn. Theo hears the thorn whispering their name. POV Theo. Beat: terrible homecoming.

chapters.title: Sefa's Map
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals she was hired to guide someone to Vaelmora—a stranger who paid in crown coin. Trust fractures. POV Sefa. Beat: betrayal suspected before confirmed.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Chapel
chapters.summary: In a flooded chapel, Theo meets Wren Calloway, a defrocked priest who knows the old oaths and claims to have served Theo's grandfather. POV Wren. Beat: hope shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Lessons in Drowned Tongues
chapters.summary: Wren begins teaching Theo the three oaths: Binding, Unbinding, and the forbidden third whose name no text records. POV Theo. Beat: hunger for knowledge, fear of cost.

chapters.title: Ostrev Follows
chapters.summary: Ostrev tracks Theo to the marsh edge, executing a gifted child found en route. His POV shows conviction curdling into zealotry. Beat: the hunt turns murderous.

chapters.title: The Price of a Word
chapters.summary: Theo practices the Binding Oath and ages visibly—each spoken word draws from their own years. The price of survival made literal. POV Theo. Beat: horror at the arithmetic of power.

chapters.title: Sefa Chooses
chapters.summary: Sefa confesses she took the crown coin to buy her family out of debtors' prison, then tears up the map and stays anyway. POV Sefa. Beat: forgiveness earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Thorn Speaks
chapters.summary: Deep in Vaelmora, the thorn addresses Theo directly, offering memories of every Villalobos who bound it—including a version of events that contradicts Ilsa's story. POV Theo. Beat: identity shaken to the root.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Last Letter
chapters.summary: A courier delivers Ilsa's final page, written as soldiers closed in: the truth—that the Villalobos line were not heroes but jailers who stole the binding from another family. POV letter/Ilsa. Beat: devastating inheritance.

chapters.title: The Other Bloodline
chapters.summary: Wren admits he serves the dispossessed family, the Amarels, who want the thorn unbound to reclaim their stolen legacy. POV Wren. Beat: ally revealed as agent.

chapters.title: Caught Between Oaths
chapters.summary: Amarel agents capture Theo, demanding the Unbinding. Theo learns the thorn drowned a kingdom when last freed. POV Theo. Beat: claustrophobic moral corner.

chapters.title: Escape by Water
chapters.summary: Sefa engineers a escape through the flooded catacombs; Wren lets them go, torn between duty and conscience. POV Sefa. Beat: loyalty tested under pressure.

chapters.title: Ostrev's Offer
chapters.summary: Ostrev corners Theo but offers terms instead of arrest: speak the Binding and serve the crown, and the surviving villagers of Thornvale go free. POV Ostrev. Beat: temptation wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: The Village Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo finds the survivors imprisoned and sees the cost of refusal written in faces. They don't know what Theo is; some beg them to accept. POV Theo. Beat: guilt weaponized.

chapters.title: A Word Spent Freely
chapters.summary: To prove good faith and buy time, Theo uses the gift openly for the first time—healing a dying prisoner at the cost of a year of life. POV Theo. Beat: agency reclaimed through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren defects fully, revealing the Amarels plan to force the Unbinding during the coronation eclipse, using Theo's captured blood as the key. POV Wren. Beat: redemption offered, uncertain.

chapters.title: The Eclipse Road
chapters.summary: Race to the capital ahead of the eclipse; Sefa navigates crown checkpoints using her old commission. POV Sefa. Beat: momentum, camaraderie, ticking clock.

chapters.title: Coronation Eve
chapters.summary: The capital glittering and afraid; anti-gift riots in the streets. Theo sees how the realm would treat a known speaker. POV Theo. Beat: foreboding amid splendor.

chapters.title: Blood in the Crypt
chapters.summary: The Amarels take Theo beneath the cathedral; the stolen blood begins the Unbinding early. The thorn's voice grows deafening. POV Theo. Beat: trap sprung, despair.

chapters.title: Ostrev's Choice
chapters.summary: Ostrev discovers the Amarel plot means the crown loses control entirely; he breaks his orders and frees Theo, choosing lesser evil over righteous certainty. POV Ostrev. Beat: antagonist transformed.

chapters.title: The First Oath Fails
chapters.summary: Theo attempts the Binding mid-ritual, but the thorn rejects it—it will only bind to willing flesh, freely given. POV Theo. Beat: all plans collapse.

chapters.title: The Third Oath
chapters.summary: Remembering the unnamed oath, Theo understands: it was never recorded because each speaker must write it themselves. Theo composes theirs aloud as the eclipse peaks. POV Theo. Beat: transcendent clarity.

chapters.title: Drowned Kingdom, Waking Thorn
chapters.summary: The thorn erupts across the capital as the partial Unbinding completes; chaos, deaths, the king's guard broken. POV ensemble. Beat: climax—consequences made visible.

chapters.title: What Theo Paid
chapters.summary: The new oath takes hold: the thorn now lives in Theo's blood, dormant but present forever. Theo has aged decades in a night. POV Theo. Beat: victory indistinguishable from loss.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Crown
chapters.summary: The regent offers Theo a title and gilded cage; Theo refuses both, negotiating amnesty for the gifted and the Amarel survivors instead. POV Theo. Beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Sefa's New Map
chapters.summary: Sefa charts safe passage for hunted gifted families toward sanctuaries; she and part ways as partners, not dependents. POV Sefa. Beat: bittersweet farewell.

chapters.title: Ostrev Resigns
chapters.summary: Ostrev surrenders his commission, unable to serve a crown that burned villages; he becomes an unlikely witness for the gifted at tribunal. POV Ostrev. Beat: atonement begun.

chapters.title: Return to Thornvale
chapters.summary: Theo walks home through the rebuilt valley where magic still cannot follow—but now carries it inside, a contradiction only they embody. POV Theo. Beat: homecoming as transformation.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Oath
chapters.summary: Years later framing device: Theo tends the thorn's offshoots, teaching a gifted orphan the discipline of words without teaching the oaths yet. POV Theo. Beat: inheritance reimagined as stewardship.

chapters.title: The Drowned Thorn
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Theo stands at the valley border at dusk, feeling the thorn pulse gently within, and speaks a single word to the dark—not an oath, just a name. POV Theo. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, story closed.
